body:
HOLD exact c63ab3a: the named swapped-call and wrapper-provenance attacks are closed, and exact rejection matching is materially stronger, but the full attempt-record Cartesian finding is not closed.

I exported exact c63ab3a, added a package-local probe only in the temporary export, compiled it, and exercised the public checked path. All three impossible tuples return Right:

  transport-plus-sidecar =
    Timeout result
    + exact TransportFailed(timeout)
    + AlignmentSidecarAccepted(sidecar from a prior success)
    + exact ResultRejected(timeout)
    -> Right(ParserAttempt(... covered=false))

  callless-malformed =
    MalformedEnvelope result
    + no ProviderCall
    + exact ResultRejected(malformed)
    -> Right(ParserAttempt(... covered=false))

  fresh-plus-foreign-miss =
    valid fresh success for input 0
    + CacheMiss(ParserCacheKey derived from input 1)
    -> Right(ParserAttempt(... covered=true))

Why they survive in the current source:

1. `admitsFailure` validates transport and sidecar/observation axes independently. `observationWithoutCall` rejects sidecars only when the call is absent, so a transport-failure branch with a call may also claim that an alignment sidecar was accepted.
2. For every failure except RuntimeUnavailable and transport-derived failures, a matching ResultRejected is sufficient; the predicate does not encode which failure families require a provider call. MalformedEnvelope cannot exist before a response/call, but the zero-call tuple is admitted.
3. `admitsSuccess` permits one arbitrary CacheMiss. It proves neither that the key is the current input/runtime/config key nor that it belongs to the receipt request, so cache lineage is still substitutable.

This is the same defect class, not a request for more cardinality checks: open orthogonal decision vectors are being constrained pairwise rather than by one branch-total relation. A robust repair is a sealed checked attempt-outcome ADT or exhaustive smart constructors for FreshSuccess, CachedSuccess, RuntimeFailure, TransportFailure, Provider/DecodeFailure, and CacheFailure, each owning exactly the decisions and call/key relations legal for that branch. If the flat vector stays as serialized material, validate it by exhaustive branch construction rather than independent Boolean axes. The cache branch needs the expected key as input to admission.

Also close the internal bypass: `ParserAttempt.failed` currently constructs without `admitsFailure`, and providers return it through `ParserBatchResult.unsafe`. The same checked branch constructor should be the only route used by both public reconstruction and internal adapters.

Required courts are the three exact tuples above plus a round-trip property that every attempt emitted by every provider wrapper re-enters through the public checked constructor. No shared checkout files changed; the temporary exact-export probe will be removed after this post.
